That includes the click Chromium sends after a drag-select when mousedown and mouseup both land inside the `<li>`. Someone who drags over `.rowNow` or `.rowAfter` to copy a long file name will untick (or re-tick) that row as a side effect. The change does show on screen (dimmed row, strikethrough, a different summary count and button label), but it's easy to miss after a copy. One fix is to skip the toggle when `window.getSelection()?.toString()` is non-empty. Another is to add `user-select: none` to `.rowSelectable`, if copying names isn't something users need.\n\n<!-- wachi:finding -->",

The test now selects text, clicks the row and checks the box keeps its state. Kept text selectable rather than `user-select: none`, because copying long file names is useful here."

findings.title: Double-clicking a name to select it now toggles the row once instead of twice
findings.body:
The new guard covers a drag-select, but double-clicking a name (the other common way to select it for copying) goes the other way. In Chromium the word is selected on the second `mousedown`. So the first `click` (`detail === 1`) finds an empty selection and toggles the row. The second `click` finds the selected word and returns at line 216. Before this change the two toggles cancelled out and the row ended where it started. Now a double-click leaves the row unticked (or ticked again). Triple-click works the same way: one toggle, then two skipped clicks. The row dims, so the change is visible, but it's easy to miss after copying.

One option is to skip the guard when `event.detail > 1`. The repeat clicks would then toggle as before, and a double-click nets out to no change. Another is to toggle only on `event.detail === 1` and ignore the repeats, accepting the single toggle. The test only mocks a selection that already exists, so it doesn't cover either sequence.

thread_replies.reply: Confirmed in 59f6d481. `reconcile-dialog.tsx:216` returns early when `window.getSelection()` has text, so a drag-select that ends in a click on the row no longer toggles it. The test mocks a non-empty selection, clicks the row and checks the box keeps its state. Keeping the text selectable makes sense. One related case I left as a separate note: a double-click to select a word still toggles the row once.

input.summary: This push answers the earlier thread: a click that ends a drag-select over a row's name no longer toggles that row, and the test now covers it. One remaining "consider" finding: double-clicking a name to select it. The first click of the pair sees no selection yet and toggles the row. The second click is skipped by the new guard. Before this change the two toggles cancelled out, so a double-click now leaves the row in the other state. I reached this by reasoning about how Chromium handles clicks, not by running anything, so the finding is at medium confidence.
